site.name: tessera
site.summary: Tessera Fictional embedded SQL database official docs and function reference (PostgreSQL / DuckDB official-docs style). Pages - `index.html` — Docs home. Hero (title + slogan + Get started button + real syntax-highlighted SELECT SQL example); version switcher (v2.4 / v2.3 / v2.2 / v2.1); ⌘K search; three quick-start cards (Install / Connect / Your first query); 6 docs-section cards (Architecture / SQL Syntax / Functions / Data Types / Storage / Extensions); dark / light theme toggle. - `reference.html` — Reference main entry. **Three-column layout**: left deep TOC tree (Schemas / Tables / Views / Indexes / Functions [Aggregate / String / Numeric / Date-Time / JSON / Window sub-groups] / Operators [category sub-groups], nodes expandable / collapsible); center reference overview + popular links + v2.4 new-features callout; right-side on-this-page outline. - `function-date-trunc.html` — DATE_TRUNC function detail page (**canonical example spec**). Three-column layout; signature code block; parameter table; return value; 3 SQL examples with result tables (basic usage / GROUP BY pairing / nested EXTRACT); error-case callouts; collapsible version-history panel (added v1.0, microsecond un

explored_user_goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the full tessera system, prioritizing the primary docs/tutorial flow plus adjacent pages, states, and recovery paths.
exploration_summary: Tessera’s docs are generally easy to orient within once a real page loads: the homepage CTA path works, reference pages have clear titles, and function/detail pages use a strong scan-friendly structure. However, several highly visible controls and links behave like placeholders or appear inert, which creates trust problems because users are invited to click paths that do not go anywhere or give no feedback. Mobile usability also needs attention: the docs show horizontal overflow, small tap targets, and an unlabeled version selector, while global search has a blocking overlay failure that harms recovery.

exploration_plan.goal: Exhaustively explore Tessera’s docs experience by validating the homepage-to-reference journey, the deep reference/navigation model, representative detail pages, and shared utility controls across desktop and mobile.
exploration_plan.summary: Start on the docs home to confirm the primary entry points into the reference and SQL syntax content, then move into the three-column reference experience where most of the system’s complexity appears to live. From there, traverse a representative set of detail pages spanning SQL syntax, data types, operators, and multiple function categories, while checking shared controls such as search, theme toggle, version switcher, TOC expansion, on-this-page navigation, copy actions, and collapsible history panels. Finish with focused mobile passes on the homepage and the dense reference/detail layouts, since the prescan already shows small tap targets and a missing label on the version selector.
assumptions: The main user flow is landing on index.html and then navigating into reference.html or sql-select.html via prominent homepage CTAs/cards.
Most pages share a common global header with version switcher, search trigger, and theme toggle, so issues there will likely repeat across the site.
reference.html and the function/detail pages use a three-column docs layout with expandable left navigation and a right-side on-this-page outline.
Some homepage and nav links intentionally point to '#' placeholders, so they should be treated as dead-end or non-navigating states rather than missing discovered pages.
Buttons visible on function and SQL pages likely include copy-code and collapsible controls; these should be validated where present rather than assumed elsewhere.
risk_hotspots: index.html header controls: version switcher has a prescan missing-label warning and several header items are below mobile tap-target guidance
index.html primary CTA set: 'Get started →' appears to use '#' and may create a broken or non-progressing primary flow
reference.html three-column layout: dense left TOC tree plus right on-this-page rail may create overflow, focus, or orientation issues
reference.html expandable/collapsible nav groups for Functions and Operators: high risk for hidden-state, discoverability, and keyboard/mobile usability issues
function-date-trunc.html version-history panel: collapsible content and error-callout sections deserve deeper state validation
sql-select.html code examples/copy actions: verify copy buttons, long code block readability, and heading/outline sync
All function detail pages: consistency of signature, parameter table, examples, errors, and version history across categories
Theme toggle across pages: verify persistence/visual stability in code blocks, tables, and sidebars after switching
Search trigger '⌘ K Search': high-value global utility worth checking for open/close behavior and graceful recovery if non-functional
Mobile on dense docs pages: repeated small tap targets in header/nav and likely cramped side navigation/outline behavior

Exercise the version switcher and observe whether selection changes page content, URL, or state
Open the search control from the homepage and validate whether it launches an overlay, focuses an input, or fails silently
Toggle theme and confirm visible styling updates on hero text, code sample, and buttons

Non-navigating placeholder links are identified and distinguished from actual UX defects

coverage_targets.pages: Visit all 9 known HTML pages, with deeper repeat passes on index.html, reference.html, sql-select.html, data-types.html, and function-date-trunc.html.
coverage_targets.features: Exercise all visible global controls at least once where present, validate major navigation paths from homepage and reference hub, and interact with most visible stateful controls on representative detail pages.
coverage_targets.mobile: Repeat critical checks on index.html and reference.html plus at least three dense content pages; prioritize header controls, expandable navigation, code/table readability, and tap-target usability.

notes: Prioritize real linked destinations over '#' placeholders to avoid spending excessive steps on intentionally static demo links.
Because the site is a local docs demo with no forms or backend flows in prescan, favor navigation, orientation, consistency, and readability over transactional testing.
Use function-date-trunc.html as the canonical deep-detail benchmark, then compare other function pages against it for consistency gaps.

findings.user_goal: Use search to jump directly to a known function or topic
findings.problem: The global search overlay can trap users in a blocked state: tapping visible results does not navigate, and the overlay intercepts interaction instead of cleanly selecting the result or closing.
findings.evidence: On desktop, clicking search results like ARRAY_AGG and DATE_TRUNC failed with repeated errors that "#cmdkOverlay intercepts pointer events," while the page stayed dimmed and the URL did not change. On mobile, tapping DATE_ADD from search on function-date-trunc.html also timed out because the same overlay intercepted pointer events, and pressing Escape did not clearly dismiss the search state.
findings.why_it_matters: Search is a primary shortcut in docs. When it opens successfully but then blocks result selection and recovery, users lose confidence and may feel stuck, especially on mobile where screen space is already limited.
findings.suggestion: Make result rows directly selectable above the backdrop, ensure the overlay has a reliable close path, and provide clear dismissal/selection behavior for both pointer and keyboard users.
findings.source_hint: Global search overlay (#cmdkOverlay) on index.html, operators.html, reference.html, function-date-trunc.html

findings.user_goal: Follow prominent homepage/reference links to learn or continue setup
findings.problem: Many prominent links look actionable but are actually dead ends with href="#", giving no unavailable-state message or alternate path.
findings.evidence: Homepage Quick start cards Install, Connect, and Your first query did not navigate and remained on index.html/index.html#. The homepage Architecture card also did nothing. On reference.html, ARRAY_AGG changed the URL only to reference.html#, while visible shortcut chips like CREATE TABLE and ALTER TABLE are also listed with href="#". Top-nav items like GitHub, Tutorials, and Download were observed as placeholder links too.
findings.why_it_matters: Users interpret large cards and header links as trustworthy entry points. Repeated silent no-ops make the docs feel unfinished and undermine confidence in the information architecture.
findings.suggestion: Remove placeholder affordances from production-like surfaces, or replace them with disabled styling plus explanatory text such as “Coming soon.” If destinations exist, wire them up consistently.
findings.source_hint: index.html quick start/documentation cards; reference.html popular links; header nav links

findings.user_goal: Understand where I am in the docs and what section is currently active
findings.problem: Active-state styling in the left navigation can highlight the wrong item, so the sidebar does not reliably reflect the current page.
findings.evidence: On function-date-trunc.html, MAX appeared highlighted while the page heading was DATE_TRUNC. On operators.html#arith, REGEXP_MATCH remained highlighted even though the main content was the Operators page. Earlier observations also noted COUNT highlighted after clicking placeholder ARRAY_AGG.
findings.why_it_matters: In a dense docs IA, users depend on the sidebar to confirm location. Incorrect active states create disorientation and reduce confidence when moving across function, operator, and syntax pages.
findings.suggestion: Tie active styling strictly to the loaded page/anchor and clear stale highlights when crossing categories or following placeholder links.
findings.source_hint: Left reference navigation on function-date-trunc.html, operators.html, reference.html

findings.user_goal: Read function docs comfortably on a phone
findings.problem: Mobile pages have horizontal overflow, causing tables and examples to clip beyond the viewport instead of fitting or clearly scrolling within their own container.
findings.evidence: On mobile function-date-trunc.html, layout warnings reported page width 443px vs viewport 390px, and the Parameters table’s Description column was visibly clipped to the right. The mobile homepage and mobile reference page also showed overflow warnings (407px on a 390px viewport).
findings.why_it_matters: Horizontal overflow makes technical content harder to read and compare, especially parameter tables and examples that are essential for successful docs use.
findings.suggestion: Constrain wide content to local scroll containers, reduce table density on small screens, and ensure the page itself does not exceed viewport width.
findings.source_hint: Mobile function-date-trunc.html parameters/examples; mobile index.html and reference.html screenshots

findings.user_goal: Understand and operate global controls like version switching
findings.problem: The version selector has no label, aria-label, or placeholder, so its purpose is unclear to assistive tech users and weaker for sighted users in a dense header.
findings.evidence: Layout warnings repeatedly flagged the select on reference.html, function-date-trunc.html, function-json-extract.html, and mobile pages as "missing_input_label." The control appears in the crowded top bar as only the version text string.
findings.why_it_matters: A release/version switcher is an important context-setting control in documentation. Without a label, users may not know what changes when they use it, and screen-reader users may receive poor or ambiguous context.
findings.suggestion: Add a clear accessible label such as “Documentation version,” and visually reinforce what the control changes.
findings.source_hint: Header version select on index.html, reference.html, and function pages

findings.user_goal: Change site theme or docs version and trust that the change happened
findings.problem: Global controls like theme toggle and version switcher often appear non-responsive because they provide little or no visible confirmation after interaction.
findings.evidence: Clicking the theme toggle on operators.html, index.html, and mobile function-date-trunc.html produced no detectable visible-text or URL change. Selecting v2.3 on operators.html and mobile function-date-trunc.html updated the control value but showed no obvious page/content change, making the switch appear inert.
findings.why_it_matters: When global controls do not visibly acknowledge input, users question whether the click/tap registered or whether the control is broken.
findings.suggestion: Provide immediate state feedback: visibly switch theme styling, update a version badge/page notice, or show a short confirmation that the selected version is now active.
findings.source_hint: Header theme toggle and version select across index.html, operators.html, function-date-trunc.html

findings.user_goal: Tap navigation and utility controls accurately on mobile
findings.problem: Many controls are undersized for touch, especially in the header and around code examples.
findings.evidence: Layout warnings repeatedly flagged controls below 44px height: mobile theme toggle 42x37, many header items around 33–37px high, homepage CTAs 38px tall, and Copy buttons on mobile examples only 46x22. Even popular reference links on mobile are 318x42, just below guidance.
findings.why_it_matters: Small targets increase mistaps and make the interface feel fiddly, especially in a docs product where users repeatedly use search, theme, version, and copy actions.
findings.suggestion: Increase tap target height/padding for top-bar controls, CTA buttons, sidebar/list links, and copy actions to meet mobile touch guidance.
findings.source_hint: Mobile index.html, reference.html, and function-date-trunc.html layout warnings

findings.problem: Copy actions do not provide clear success feedback, so users cannot tell whether code was actually copied.
findings.evidence: On mobile function-date-trunc.html, tapping the visible Copy button produced no visible feedback and the label remained "Copy" afterward. Earlier attempts to evaluate copy on other pages were interrupted by navigation, so the only direct evidence still suggests weak confirmation behavior.
findings.why_it_matters: Copy is a high-value docs action. Without confirmation, users may recopy, manually select text, or distrust the examples.
findings.suggestion: Show a clear transient success state such as “Copied” with an icon or toast, and keep the control comfortably tappable.

gaps: Only directly exercised 9% of visible interactive feature signatures.
5 browser action(s) failed and should be retried or analyzed.
